instructions: Overture is a single-owner job-application agent: Bun + TypeScript, Hono on Bun, Drizzle ORM over SQLite (app.sqlite + catalog.sqlite, one machine, Litestream), Zod contracts shared between server and web, React 19 + React Query + Tailwind v4 (CSS-first @theme in src/web/styles.css, Ember design system) and Radix/shadcn primitives. Banned in product copy and code: Hold (as a stage), runner, lease, provider, dispatch, attempt, ledger, credit, CAPTCHA, Brain, Hands. The tools are the rules: bun lint, bun fmt --check, bun check, bun test src, bun run build, bun run lint:config and bun run db:verify must pass; never suggest silencing a rule, skipping a test or passing --no-verify as a fix. Ignore generated files, migration snapshots, design reference PNGs and build output.

rules.rule: Any write that can race another connection must run inside db.transaction(callback, { behavior: "immediate" }), with a synchronous callback using .run(), and retryWhenBusy around chunked writers. A db.transaction(async ...) callback is a bug: drizzle/bun-sqlite commits before the awaited writes run. Flag deferred transactions on write paths.

Every query and mutation that returns or changes a person's data must filter on the session user id from readSession/readSessionUser, never on a client-supplied id. The demo account is read-only: its writes must be refused on the server, not only hidden in the UI.

A change may not weaken the quality bar: no new oxlint/eslint disable comments, no --no-verify, no skipped, deleted or trivialised tests, no removed assertions, no threshold edited down, no unimplemented stub left behind. If a rule is wrong, it needs an ADR, not a suppression.

Migrations are additive and one per pull request: create table/index/column only, no drops or renames without an expand/contract plan, and the drizzle/meta journal entry must match the .sql file name and index. A destructive change needs an ADR and a backup/restore step.

Money paths must be idempotent and must not leak or double-charge: Stripe calls carry an Idempotency-Key, webhook events are claimed once before they write, an attempt's ledger reservation is released on every failure/abort/shutdown path, and a refund or status transition is guarded by the status it expects. Flag any path where a retry or crash can bill twice or strand a reservation.

Never log, return in a response, or persist unencrypted a secret, token, session cookie, Stripe key, or another person's personal data. Server logs go through logInfo/logError, not console. Ciphertext that cannot be opened must degrade to a null/empty result with a logged error, not a 500 that leaks the ciphertext.

The web app uses the Ember tokens and the shared primitives in src/web/components/ui only: no raw hex/rgba colours, no arbitrary text sizes on product routes, no off-scale spacing in the strict paths enforced by overture/no-raw-design-styles. Interactive elements need a visible focus ring, a 44px touch target on phones, and an accessible name.

Check the pull request description's claims against the diff: a summary that says a test, guard, header or migration exists must point at one that does. Report documentation drift in docs/SPEC.md, docs/DEPLOY.md, DESIGN.md, GLOSSARY.md or an ADR when behaviour changed without them.
